system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Berlin, Germany. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Berlin itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Berlin space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Mitte, Kreuzberg, Charlottenburg, Schöneberg) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Berlin spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Berlin, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Sprüth Magers
galleries.note: Blue-chip powerhouse (Cologne roots, global spaces) representing Rosemarie Trockel, Cyprien Gaillard, Barbara Kruger and Andreas Gursky; the benchmark of Berlin's commercial scene.

galleries.name: Esther Schipper
galleries.note: Home of relational-aesthetics era figures such as Philippe Parreno, Pierre Huyghe, Ryan Gander and Ann Veronica Janssens; huge biennale and fair presence.

galleries.name: neugerriemschneider
galleries.note: Founded 1994; Olafur Eliasson, Ai Weiwei, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Thomas Bayrle — one of the galleries that made post-Wall Berlin internationally legible.

galleries.name: Galerie Max Hetzler
galleries.note: Historic German dealer with several Berlin spaces plus Paris and London; Albert Oehlen, Bridget Riley, Rebecca Warren and a strong painting roster.

galleries.name: KW Institute for Contemporary Art
galleries.note: The city's key kunsthalle-style institution, birthplace of the Berlin Biennale and a launchpad for generations of artists and curators.

galleries.name: Galerie Eigen + Art
galleries.note: Judy Lybke's gallery brought the Leipzig School (Neo Rauch, Tim Eitel) west; a defining presence on Auguststraße since the 1990s.

galleries.name: Galerie Buchholz
galleries.note: Rigorously art-historical programme (Wolfgang Tillmans, Isa Genzken, Lutz Bacher estate); Cologne/Berlin/New York with outsized critical weight.

galleries.name: Capitain Petzel
galleries.note: Joint venture of Gisela Capitain and Friedrich Petzel in a landmark GDR modernist glass pavilion; Wade Guyton, Charline von Heyl, Sarah Morris.

galleries.name: Contemporary Fine Arts
galleries.note: Founded 1992; painting-heavy roster tied to Georg Baselitz, Daniel Richter, Jonathan Meese and Tal R.

galleries.name: König Galerie
galleries.note: Johann König's brutalist church space is a Berlin landmark; Katharina Grosse, Alicja Kwade, Jorinde Voigt and a large-scale sculptural programme.

galleries.name: Galerie Neu
galleries.note: Influential since 1994; a discreet, critically respected programme including Klara Lidén, Manfred Pernice and Sergej Jensen.

galleries.name: Barbara Wien
galleries.note: Gallery and art bookshop devoted to conceptual practices — Tomas Schmit, Haegue Yang, Nanne Meyer — with deep scholarly credibility.

galleries.name: Galerie Isabella Bortolozzi
galleries.note: Idiosyncratic, much-imitated programme (Danh Vo, Wu Tsang, Ed Atkins, Anna Uddenberg) that shaped 2010s Berlin taste.

galleries.name: carlier | gebauer
galleries.note: Berlin and Madrid; strong film and photography emphasis with Paul Pfeiffer, Iñigo Manglano-Ovalle and Aslı Çavuşoğlu.

galleries.name: Konrad Fischer Galerie
galleries.note: Berlin outpost of the legendary Düsseldorf gallery of Minimal, Conceptual and Arte Povera art; Hanne Darboven, Gregor Schneider, Thomas Ruff.

galleries.name: Schinkel Pavillon
galleries.note: Nina Pohl's octagonal 1960s pavilion; ambitious, widely reviewed exhibitions that operate at museum level on a kunstverein budget.

galleries.name: Galerie Nagel Draxler
galleries.note: Cologne-rooted gallery with a politically engaged, institutional-critique lineage (Andrea Fraser, Cosima von Bonin, Merlin Carpenter).

galleries.name: Galerie Thomas Schulte
galleries.note: Longstanding programme of American and European conceptual and post-minimal artists — Gordon Matta-Clark estate, Alfredo Jaar, Rebecca Horn.

galleries.name: Société
galleries.note: Defining gallery of post-internet and technology-driven art: Timur Si-Qin, Petra Cortright, Bunny Rogers.

galleries.name: Neuer Berliner Kunstverein (n.b.k.)
galleries.note: Kunstverein with a major video-art archive and artothek; consistently rigorous exhibitions and discourse programmes since 1969.

galleries.name: Kraupa-Tuskany Zeidler
galleries.note: Barometer of emerging digital, speculative and post-humanist practices; Yuri Pattison, Jenna Sutela, Nora Turato-adjacent generation.

galleries.name: Peres Projects
galleries.note: Javier Peres's aggressively international gallery (also Milan, Seoul) that helped launch a wave of young figurative painters.

galleries.name: Galerie Barbara Weiss
galleries.note: Founded 1992 and continued after Weiss's death; Maria Eichhorn, Ceal Floyer, Peter Wächtler — a cornerstone of conceptual Berlin.

galleries.name: Mehdi Chouakri
galleries.note: Since 1996 a champion of conceptual and geometric traditions: Sylvie Fleury, John Armleder, Charlotte Posenenske estate.

galleries.name: Kewenig
galleries.note: Baroque Palais in old Mitte housing Jannis Kounellis, Joseph Kosuth and Bosco Sodi; also Palma de Mallorca.

galleries.name: ChertLüdde
galleries.note: Merger of Chert and Lüdde; research-driven programme rediscovering figures like Gabriele Stötzer alongside Monia Ben Hamouda and Kasia Fudakowski.

galleries.name: Julia Stoschek Foundation Berlin
galleries.note: Free public exhibitions from one of the world's leading collections of time-based and moving-image art.

galleries.name: Galerie Nordenhake
galleries.note: Stockholm-born gallery in Berlin since 2000; Ann Edholm, Esther Kläs, Miroslaw Balka and a strong Nordic-international bridge.

galleries.name: Meyer Riegger
galleries.note: Karlsruhe/Berlin/Basel gallery with Miriam Cahn, Stef Heidhues and a consistently strong fair presence.

galleries.name: Tanya Leighton
galleries.note: Sharp cross-generational programme (Sam Pulitzer, Oliver Osborne, Math Bass) with a second Los Angeles space.

galleries.name: KINDL – Centre for Contemporary Art
galleries.note: Former brewery converted into a large privately funded kunsthalle known for spectacular site-specific commissions in the Boiler House.

galleries.name: Galerie Judin
galleries.note: Juerg Judin's gallery pairs contemporary painting with scholarly historical shows (Tom of Finland, Peter Saul, Norbert Bisky).

galleries.name: Wentrup
galleries.note: Reliable mid-size gallery with Gregor Hildebrandt, Axel Geis and Thomas Wachholz; active on the international fair circuit.

galleries.name: Galerie Barbara Thumm
galleries.note: Since 1997; feminist and globally minded roster including Teresa Burga estate, Anna Oppermann estate and Fernando Bryce.

galleries.name: Klemm's
galleries.note: Photography- and conceptually-oriented programme (Sven Johne, Adrian Sauer, Viktoria Binschtok) with steady critical attention.

galleries.name: Künstlerhaus Bethanien
galleries.note: International studio residency programme since 1975 with public exhibition spaces; a main gateway into Berlin for foreign artists.

galleries.name: Buchmann Galerie
galleries.note: Swiss-founded gallery of postwar and contemporary sculpture and painting: Tony Cragg, Fiona Rae, Bettina Pousttchi.

galleries.name: Galerie Guido W. Baudach
galleries.note: Grew out of the legendary Maschenmode project space; Thomas Zipp, Erwin Kneihsl, André Butzer's early years.

galleries.name: daadgalerie
galleries.note: Exhibition space of the DAAD Artists-in-Berlin Programme, the residency that has brought many of the world's leading artists to the city.

galleries.name: BQ
galleries.note: Cologne-founded gallery with a lean conceptual roster including Michael Krebber-adjacent painters and Andreas Slominski.

galleries.name: Sammlung Boros
galleries.note: Private collection in a WWII bunker, shown to the public in multi-year rotations; a fixture of every Berlin art itinerary.

galleries.name: SAVVY Contemporary
galleries.note: Discursive 'laboratory of form-ideas' led by Bonaventure Soh Bejeng Ndikung; internationally influential in decolonial curating.

galleries.name: Galeria Plan B
galleries.note: Cluj gallery whose Berlin space introduced the Romanian painting scene (Adrian Ghenie, Navid Nuur, Belu-Simion Făinaru) to a wider public.

galleries.name: C/O Berlin
galleries.note: Foundation-run photography kunsthalle with major monographic shows and the C/O Berlin Talent Award.

galleries.name: Dittrich & Schlechtriem
galleries.note: Ambitious younger-generation gallery known for Julian Charrière, Andreas Greiner and science-adjacent installation work.

galleries.name: Sweetwater
galleries.note: Small, critically watched gallery whose experimental programme punches far above its size on the international scene.

galleries.name: Efremidis
galleries.note: Large-format gallery in a modernist office building showing emerging international artists in ambitious solo presentations.

galleries.name: Zilberman
galleries.note: Istanbul-based gallery whose Berlin space is a key node for Turkish and Middle Eastern contemporary art in Germany.

galleries.name: Kicken Berlin
galleries.note: One of the world's most important photography dealers since 1974: Bauhaus, avant-garde and classic modern photography.

galleries.name: Persons Projects
galleries.note: Timothy Persons's gallery built around the Helsinki School; the main Berlin address for contemporary Nordic photography.

galleries.name: nGbK – neue Gesellschaft für bildende Kunst
galleries.note: Member-run, collectively curated art association since 1969; a model of political and participatory exhibition-making.

galleries.name: Galerie Crone
galleries.note: Hamburg-founded gallery, now Berlin and Vienna, with a long history of supporting German painting and performance-based practices.

galleries.name: Soy Capitán
galleries.note: Well-regarded younger gallery with a strong focus on drawing, textile and female-led practices.

galleries.name: PSM
galleries.note: Research-based, often politically engaged programme with artists from South Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

galleries.name: Haus am Waldsee
galleries.note: Villa-based international art space since 1946; mid-career survey shows of Berlin-based artists with a strong sculpture garden.

galleries.name: alexander levy
galleries.note: Gallery at the intersection of art, science and technology; known for Julius von Bismarck's early exhibitions.

galleries.name: Sexauer Gallery
galleries.note: Weissensee gallery with an experimental, discourse-heavy programme and an active writing and events series.

galleries.name: CAMERA WORK
galleries.note: Large photography gallery dealing classic and contemporary names, from Helmut Newton to contemporary fashion photography.

galleries.name: Aurel Scheibler
galleries.note: Cologne-founded dealer with a refined programme linking postwar rediscoveries to contemporary painting.

galleries.name: Kuckei + Kuckei
galleries.note: Long-running Mitte gallery with Scandinavian and German artists and a steady photography emphasis.

galleries.name: Galerie Kornfeld
galleries.note: Spacious Charlottenburg gallery showing established international modern and contemporary positions.

galleries.name: Between Bridges
galleries.note: Wolfgang Tillmans's non-profit foundation space for exhibitions and projects around social and political questions.

galleries.name: Bastian
galleries.note: Chipperfield-designed space opposite the Museumsinsel; museum-quality shows of Beuys, Twombly and postwar classics.

galleries.name: Galerie Michael Haas
galleries.note: Established West Berlin dealer of classic modern and contemporary German art, active for over four decades.

galleries.name: Fluentum
galleries.note: Private collection space for time-based media in a former Luftwaffe headquarters; commissions and residencies for film-based artists.

galleries.name: Wschód
galleries.note: Warsaw gallery with a Berlin space; a conduit for a widely watched younger Central and Eastern European generation.

galleries.name: Galerie Tanja Wagner
galleries.note: Feminist and socially engaged programme; early supporter of artists such as Christine Sun Kim's peers and Ulrike Rosenbach's legacy.

galleries.name: Robert Morat Galerie
galleries.note: Contemporary photography gallery with a documentary and book-culture orientation, active at Paris Photo and Unseen.

galleries.name: Galerie Berinson
galleries.note: Specialist in avant-garde photography and Russian/Central European modernism, a scholarly presence on Auguststraße.

galleries.name: Galerie Volker Diehl
galleries.note: Veteran Berlin dealer known for pioneering exchanges with Russian and Eastern European contemporary art.

galleries.name: Kunstraum Kreuzberg/Bethanien
galleries.note: District-funded exhibition space with thematic, socially engaged group shows in the historic Bethanien building.

galleries.name: Galerie Deschler
galleries.note: Long-established Mitte gallery showing German figurative painting, photography and video.

galleries.name: Galerie Poll
galleries.note: One of Berlin's oldest galleries (founded 1968), historically tied to critical realism and political figuration.

galleries.name: Galerie Georg Nothelfer
galleries.note: Since 1971 a champion of Informel, gesture and abstraction — K.O. Götz, Emil Schumacher, Antoni Tàpies.

galleries.name: Haverkampf Leistenschneider
galleries.note: Charlottenburg gallery showing emerging and mid-career international painters with a growing fair profile.

galleries.name: Galerie Springer Berlin
galleries.note: Continuation of the historic Rudolf Springer gallery; surrealism, photography and contemporary positions.

galleries.name: ZK/U – Center for Art and Urbanistics
galleries.note: Residency and exhibition centre in a former railway depot linking artistic practice with urban research.

galleries.name: Galerie Wedding – Raum für zeitgenössische Kunst
galleries.note: Municipal project space with a consistently sharp, politically curated programme in the town hall of Wedding.

galleries.name: Hua International
galleries.note: Beijing-linked gallery whose Berlin space shows young Chinese and international artists working with digital media.

galleries.name: Noah Klink
galleries.note: Young gallery with a tightly curated emerging programme that has become a fixture of the city's off-circuit.

galleries.name: Sandy Brown
galleries.note: Artist-run-spirited gallery known for idiosyncratic solo shows by emerging Berlin-based artists.

galleries.name: Molitor
galleries.note: Recent addition to the Berlin scene with a research-minded programme of young international artists.

galleries.name: Ebensperger
galleries.note: Vienna-rooted gallery whose atmospheric Berlin space stages unusually theatrical installations and group shows.

galleries.name: Galerie Rolando Anselmi
galleries.note: Rome/Berlin gallery presenting emerging Italian and international artists, with an eye for painting.

galleries.name: ŻAK | BRANICKA
galleries.note: Focused on Polish conceptual art and its contemporary heirs; long an important East-West bridge in Berlin.

galleries.name: Galerie Nord / Kunstverein Tiergarten
galleries.note: District art association with a socially engaged programme and long-running support for Berlin-based artists.

galleries.name: Kunstverein am Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz
galleries.note: Small artist-driven kunstverein staging concentrated solo projects in the heart of old Mitte.

galleries.name: Kreuzberg Pavillon
galleries.note: Artist-run space famed for fast-turnaround, one-evening exhibitions and a fiercely independent stance.

galleries.name: SOX
galleries.note: Shop-window space visible 24/7 from the street; a long-running, much-copied model for micro-exhibitions.

galleries.name: insitu
galleries.note: Curatorial collective producing thematic group shows and collaborations with international project spaces.

galleries.name: Horse & Pony
galleries.note: Neukölln project space and residency with a queer, community-oriented programme of exhibitions and performance.

galleries.name: After the Butcher
galleries.note: Thomas Kilpper's long-running space for art and social issues in a former butcher's shop in Lichtenberg.

galleries.name: Institut für Alles Mögliche
galleries.note: Sprawling artist-run network of free studios, residencies and exhibition rooms across several Berlin sites.

galleries.name: Rosalux
galleries.note: Artist collective and gallery running one of the city's steadiest independent exhibition programmes.

galleries.name: TROPEZ
galleries.note: Summer-season art space inside a public swimming pool; commissions, performances and a cult local following.

galleries.name: Grüntaler9
galleries.note: Tiny live-art and performance space with an internationally networked experimental programme.

galleries.name: General Public
galleries.note: Artist-run space active since 2005, known for interdisciplinary projects, sound art and residencies.

galleries.name: KUNSTSAELE Berlin
galleries.note: Collection-based exhibition venue that also hosts guest curators and young galleries in its large rooms.

galleries.name: Salon Dahlmann
galleries.note: Collector-run apartment space showing Finnish and international contemporary art to the public free of charge.

galleries.name: SomoS Art House
galleries.note: Independent art house combining residencies, performance nights and exhibitions for an international emerging community.
